newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S MOL SAYS GAS DEAL FAVOURABLE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S MOL SAYS GAS DEAL FAVOURABLE.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL) said on Friday the terms of a 20-year gas deal with Panrusgaz for the purchase of 225 billion cubic meters of natural gas are favourable for the company.
"This new agreement contains a renegotiated price from October 1996 and a new formula characterised by lower volatility," MOL said in a statement.
MOL announced the contract with Panrusgaz -- its 50-50 joint venture with Gazprom -- on November 8 but at the time neither company gave details of the deal.

"The starting price is advantageous compared to western European gas prices, the calculated price in our previous contract and compared to gas supplies to other countries in the region," the statement said.
It added that "the price remains... around $20 per thousand cubic meters higher than the current regulated wholesale price."
In the first nine months of 1996 MOL imported 5.5 billion cubic meters of natural gas which it sold at state-regulated prices at a loss of 2.4 forints per cubic meter, the company said on Thursday.
The government's decision on the energy price increases that are supposed to give energy companies an eight percent return on equity is expected next Thursday.
The price increase, due to take effect on January 1, 1997, is expected to be between 20 to 25 percent.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange MOL shares finished at 1,655 forints, up five.
